title: Sausage Rolls
subtitle: Flaky pastry filled with seasoned pork
excerpt: Crisp, golden rough puff pastry wrapped around herbed pork mince. These are the kind of sausage rolls worth making from scratch. Great warm from the oven or packed into a lunchbox.
sourceNotes: Sausage rolls are a staple of British baking, believed to have evolved from French feuillete pastry brought to Britain in the 19th century. The British version filled with seasoned pork mince became a fixture at bakeries and market stalls across the country.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and refrigerate overnight, then egg wash and bake just before serving.

content.text: Keep the butter cold throughout the pastry process. If the kitchen is warm, chill the dough for 10 minutes between folds to keep the layers distinct.

Make the rough puff pastry. Put the flour in a bowl and add the cold butter cubes. Use your fingertips to flatten each cube into the flour without rubbing it in fully. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water and bring together into a shaggy dough. On a floured surface, roll to a rectangle about 20 by 40 cm. Fold the top third down, then the bottom third up (like a letter). Rotate 90 degrees and repeat the roll and fold once more. Wrap and chill for 20 minutes.
Mix the pork mince with the grated onion, sage, mustard, a generous pinch of salt, and some black pepper. Squeeze the mixture together until well combined.
Preheat the oven to 200 C. Roll the chilled pastry on a floured surface to a rectangle roughly 30 by 40 cm. Cut into two long strips, each about 15 cm wide.

Divide the filling in two and shape each half into a long log down the centre of each pastry strip. Brush one edge of each strip with egg wash, then fold the pastry over the filling and press to seal. Crimp with a fork. Cut each roll into 6 pieces and place on the baking tray. Brush the tops with egg wash and score each roll with two cuts.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Butter was too warm or dough was overworked
items.fix: Keep butter cold and handle dough as little as possible.

items.cause: Seal was not pressed firmly enough
items.fix: Press the edge firmly and crimp with a fork to hold it shut.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough or tray too crowded
items.fix: Space rolls on the tray and check oven is fully preheated.
